correctness.rationale: The canonical regular simplex has facet volume sqrt(N-1)/(N-2)! and normal projections sqrt(N/(N-1)) U_i. Cauchy brightness formula gives Y=sqrt(N/(N-1)) sum |U_i|, while crossed edges give section vertices C=p(N-p). Equal positive/negative absolute masses a and unit norm imply 1/2<a²<=pq/N for generic N>=3 (upper equality for two-level sign classes), hence the entire half-open Y interval; connectedness of each sign chamber fills every intermediate value. The exact finite E[Y] and E[Y²] use spherical absolute-coordinate and correlated Gaussian pair moments. Represent U by centered iid Gaussians divided by their Euclidean norm. The sign-count influence psi=1_(G>0)-1/2-phi(0)G is odd and has variance s²; the brightness influence eta=|G|-sqrt(2/pi)-(sqrt(2/pi)/2)(G²-1) is even and has variance tau²=1-3/pi. Empirical moving-threshold/grid remainder and normalization errors are o_p(1), so iid bivariate CLT yields independent Gaussian limits, squaring sign count gives independent chi-square vertex deficit. Every all-N assertion is analytic, not extrapolated from finite simulations.

value.rationale: A single hyperplane produces two intrinsic observables: discrete section complexity and continuous orthogonal shadow volume. The exact feasible joint domain and equality directions answer a natural inverse-geometric compatibility question, and the independent Gaussian/chi-square limit explains why a strong deterministic finite-N coupling disappears at fluctuation scales. These are genuinely additional joint facts beyond previously published section-only face counts and projection-only widths.
